title: What were the IRA hunger strikes?
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the IRA hunger strikes, beginning with the Irish and Northern Irish background: the 1609 plantation of Ulster, Home Rule, the 1916 Easter Rising, the Anglo-Irish War and the 1920s partition into Northern Ireland and the Irish Republic, and the Troubles from the late 1960s. They trace the Gaelic tradition of the troscad, early 20th-century hunger strikes by Irish suffragists and IRA prisoners (James Connolly, Thomas Ashe), and the 1970s prison fight over political-prisoner status, including Operation Demetrius, the criminalization policy of 1976, the blanket and dirty protests, and the five demands. They cover the 1980 hunger strike led by Bernadette McAliskey's campaign, the 1981 strike in which Bobby Sands was elected to Parliament while imprisoned and died after 66 days, the ten deaths across the 1981 strike, and how it ended on October 3, 1981 after Humphrey Atkins was replaced by James Prior. They also discuss the 2008 film Hunger, the recent Sinn Féin election result, and a listener mail segment about a squirrel story.

segments.title: Opening and Sinn Féin election context
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on IRA hunger strikes, note Sinn Féin becoming the largest party in the Northern Ireland Assembly elections, and acknowledge the sensitivity of the topic.

segments.title: Background: plantation, Home Rule and the Easter Rising
segments.summary: Overview of Irish and Northern Irish history from the 1609 plantation of Ulster through Home Rule, the 1916 Easter Rising, and the Anglo-Irish War, leading to the partition into Northern Ireland and the Irish Republic.

segments.title: The Troubles and origins of the IRA
segments.summary: The Troubles starting in the late 1960s, with about 3,500 deaths, and the origins of the IRA from the Irish Volunteers through the 1920s civil war to the Provisional IRA.

segments.title: Hunger strikes: troscad and early history
segments.summary: The Gaelic tradition of the troscad, a public hunger strike used to shame debtors, and early 20th-century hunger strikes by suffragists and IRA prisoners including James Connolly and Thomas Ashe, whose death followed forced feeding.

segments.title: Political prisoner status and criminalization
segments.summary: The fight for political-prisoner status, Operation Demetrius internment, the 1976 criminalization policy, and how the British treated IRA prisoners as criminals and why hunger strikes were effective publicity.

segments.title: Blanket protest, dirty protest and the five demands
segments.summary: Prisoners refused prison clothes and wore blankets, then began the dirty protest; guards abused prisoners; the five demands emerged, and Bernadette McAliskey supported the campaign. Discussion of the film Hunger.

segments.title: 1980 and 1981 hunger strikes and Bobby Sands
segments.summary: The October 1980 strike ended after 53 days without deaths, Thatcher's stance, the March 1981 strike led by Bobby Sands, his election to Parliament while in prison, his death after 66 days, and the ten deaths and ending of the strike on October 3, 1981.

segments.title: Closing discussion and listener mail
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the legacy of the strikes for Sinn Féin and the IRA, mention Bono's son's band, and read a listener email about a squirrel incident in Zion National Park. Sign-off.
